url_obfuscation_techniques: Use of digit '1' instead of letter 'i' in domain (m1crosoft-support.com)
HTTPS protocol with valid but self-signed certificate
Long JWT-like session token appended to URL to appear legitimate
URL parameters encoded to avoid easy detection

indicators.waf_rule_triggered: ID 950101 - Possible password in POST data

example.detection_method: Detection via advanced email filtering identifying domain similarity and SPF pass but unusual domain; WAF/IDS triggering on POST requests containing password fields; user reports from phishing simulation exercises; correlation of domain registration data with threat intelligence feeds; heuristic URL analysis for homoglyph substitution and suspicious URL parameters.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1110 - Brute Force (for credential reuse post-harvesting)

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents a credential harvesting social engineering attack via phishing. The scenario clearly describes spear-phishing emails impersonating Microsoft 365 with a visually similar domain, aligning well with the problem nature. The technical data is comprehensive and realistic, including detailed email headers, SMTP logs, phishing domain registration info, HTTP requests capturing credential submission, and WAF alerts. Indicators are clearly listed and directly support the identification of the phishing campaign. The detection methods and relevant MITRE techniques are appropriate and well-mapped to the scenario. The sample includes all required fields and populates them with plausible, consistent data. To improve, the sample could explicitly mention risk reduction measures such as MFA implementation or user training in the detection_method or comments section to better connect with the problem's risk reduction strategies. Overall, this is a high-quality, complete, and realistic example of credential harvesting via social engineering.
